subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Mars Rovers
description: A quick, practical guide to The Mars Rovers.

hook.text: NASA has landed five rovers on Mars. Each lasted far longer than designed.

buildup.text: Opportunity was built for 90 days. It drove for 14 years and 45 km across the Martian surface.

discovery.text: Curiosity found organic molecules and seasonal methane—hints that Mars may not be fully dead.

twist.text: Spirit got stuck in sand after 6 years. Its last signal was a fading whisper in the Martian winter.

climax.text: Perseverance landed in 2021 with Ingenuity—the first helicopter to fly on another planet.

punchline.text: Built for 90 days, drove for 14 years. Rovers never quit.

quiz.question: How long did the Opportunity rover operate on Mars?
options: About 14 years, far exceeding its 90-day design

details.summary: NASA's Mars rovers — Sojourner (1997), Spirit and Opportunity (2004), Curiosity (2012), and Perseverance (2021) — have driven across Mars exploring ancient terrain.
details.whyItMatters: Mars rovers are our robotic geologists on another planet, providing ground truth that orbiters cannot. Their discoveries of ancient habitable environments make the case for a Mars sample return mission — the next giant leap in planetary science.
takeaways: Five NASA rovers have explored Mars since 1997
They confirmed ancient water and habitable environments
Perseverance is collecting samples for future return to Earth

faq.question: Which Mars rover lasted the longest?
faq.answer: Opportunity operated for nearly 15 years (2004-2018), far exceeding its 90-day mission. It drove over 45 kilometers — a marathon on Mars. A planet-wide dust storm in 2018 blocked sunlight from its solar panels, ending communications. Curiosity (nuclear-powered) is still operating after 12+ years.

faq.question: What did Ingenuity achieve?
faq.answer: The 1.8-kilogram Ingenuity helicopter made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet on April 19, 2021. Originally planned for 5 flights in 30 days, it completed 72 flights over nearly 3 years before a rotor blade was damaged. It proved aerial exploration on Mars is possible.
